headline: Manchester keeps Queen City Bridge closed as inspection continues
dek: The Route 3 crossing over the Merrimack River remains closed in both directions after possible structural deficiencies were found; overnight I-293 lane restrictions are planned as engineers continue work.
body: Manchester's Queen City Bridge remains closed in both directions while officials investigate possible structural deficiencies found during a routine inspection, the city said. The bridge carries Route 3 over the Merrimack River and connects the city's east and west sides near Elliot Hospital at River's Edge.

The New Hampshire Department of Transportation notified Manchester officials on Sept. 21, and the city said a full inspection was not yet complete. New Hampshire Public Radio reported that the bridge, built in 1923, spans 1,186 feet and was last rehabilitated in 2020.

The closure is also affecting traffic near the crossing. The New Hampshire Department of Transportation plans overnight I-293 lane restrictions in the bridge area on Wednesday and Thursday as inspectors continue their work, according to WMUR. The work is scheduled for 9 p.m. to 5 a.m.; drivers entering southbound I-293 at Exit 4 are to be detoured onto Second Street to Exit 5.
There is no announced reopening date. Manchester is directing drivers to seek alternate routes while officials determine the extent of the problem and what repairs, if any, will be needed.
author: NorthEast News Desk
